fact: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission's Public Playground Safety Handbook says a surface's ASTM F1292 critical height rating should be greater than or equal to the fall height of the highest equipment, that grass and dirt are not protective surfacing, and that carpeting and mats are not appropriate unless tested to ASTM F1292.
quote: Testing using the methods described in ASTM F1292 will provide a “critical height” rating of the surface. … Manufacturers and installers of playground protective surfacing should provide the critical height rating of their materials. This rating should be greater than or equal to the fall height of the highest piece of equipment on the playground. … Grass and dirt are not considered protective surfacing because wear and environmental factors can reduce their shock absorbing effectiveness. Carpeting and mats are also not appropriate unless they are tested to and comply with ASTM F1292.
source_label: U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, Public Playground Safety Handbook (Pub. No. 325), section 2.4 Surfacing and 2.4.2 Selecting a surfacing material
notes: Read 2026-09-25 in the PDF at cpsc.gov (the 2010 handbook with the CPSC's December 29, 2015 notice on rubber mulch in front; pages 8-9). The handbook is written for public playgrounds; it is a federal recommendation, not a Colorado or town rule. Pages that apply it to a backyard playset say so. A shared record because it holds for every town.
